websites.title: Websites
websites.summary: Build a vocabulary for the web: discovery, trust, infrastructure, performance, and growth. Start with recognizable subjects that work on their own.
websites.principle: One subject. One clear meaning. Many useful aliases.

entries.name: Web globe
entries.meaning: The web as a globally connected place.
entries.brief: A freestanding globe with a few latitude and longitude lines. No browser, pointer, or surrounding orbit.
entries.why: Keep one recognizable globe; add web-related aliases.

entries.name: Compass
entries.meaning: Finding a destination or exploring content.
entries.brief: A circular compass with one integrated needle and minimal direction ticks. No map or location pin.
entries.why: A shared navigation object gives Websites a clear discovery concept.

entries.name: Anchor
entries.meaning: A stable destination within a page.
entries.brief: One nautical anchor with its ring, shank, curved arms, and flukes. No chain, page, or link badge.
entries.why: Use as a metaphor; the visual noun stays Anchor.

entries.name: Chain links
entries.meaning: A connection between web resources.
entries.brief: Two naturally interlocking chain links, treated as one piece of chain. No broken segment or status mark.
entries.why: Reuse across categories instead of drawing a category-specific link.

entries.name: Cookie
entries.meaning: Stored preferences and website tracking.
entries.brief: One round cookie with a few integrated chocolate chips and a simple bitten edge. No shield or checkmark.
entries.why: The food object already supplies the familiar web metaphor.

entries.name: Padlock
entries.meaning: Restricted access and secure content.
entries.brief: One closed padlock with an arched shackle and a plain body. No toggle, checkmark, or document.
entries.why: Replace lock-plus-toggle combinations with the reusable lock object.

entries.name: Fingerprint
entries.meaning: Biometric identity and authentication.
entries.brief: One fingertip ridge pattern, with open curved ridges forming a clear oval. No scanning frame or device.
entries.why: Inspect the original before reuse; isolate the fingerprint if needed.

entries.name: Hardware security token
entries.meaning: A physical key for signing in.
entries.brief: One compact USB security token: short body, integrated circular touch contact, and exposed USB connector. No padlock or key overlay.
entries.why: Adds a distinct physical authentication object beyond a generic key.

entries.name: Spider
entries.meaning: An automated crawler that discovers pages.
entries.brief: One spider with a compact body and eight legs. No web, magnifying glass, or browser.
entries.why: Keep Spider as the name; Web crawler belongs in aliases.

entries.name: Server rack
entries.meaning: The hardware that hosts websites.
entries.brief: One upright server rack with integrated equipment bays and small indicator lights. No wings, motion lines, or cloud.
entries.why: Reuse plain server hardware; migration is a separate action.

entries.name: Database
entries.meaning: Structured information stored for a website.
entries.brief: One cylindrical database object with two or three integrated tiers. No arrows, document, or lock.
entries.why: Use one database across Websites, Programming, and Diagrams.

entries.name: Router
entries.meaning: A device that routes network traffic.
entries.brief: One low router body with two attached antennae and a few integrated port details. No floating Wi-Fi symbol.
entries.why: A hardware noun with clear cross-category reuse.

entries.name: Network switch
entries.meaning: A device that connects wired network equipment.
entries.brief: One low rectangular network switch with an integrated row of Ethernet ports and two indicator lights. No branching arrows or separate cables.
entries.why: Adds a wired networking object distinct from an antenna router.

entries.name: Server blade
entries.meaning: An individual computing module inside a server system.
entries.brief: One slim removable server blade with an integrated front handle, ventilation slots, and a small status light. No rack or arrows.
entries.why: A specific hardware noun that broadens the server vocabulary.

entries.name: Fiber optic connector
entries.meaning: A physical connection for high-speed data.
entries.brief: One fiber connector with a narrow ferrule, squared coupling body, ribbed strain relief, and a short attached cable end. No speed lines or arrows.
entries.why: Related fiber concepts exist; inspect them before commissioning this specific connector.

entries.name: Patch panel
entries.meaning: A fixed panel for organizing network connections.
entries.brief: One slim patch panel with two mounting ears and a single integrated row of ports. No cables, labels, or separate tools.
entries.why: Provides a passive networking component with a distinct silhouette.

entries.name: Hourglass
entries.meaning: Time spent waiting for a page or process.
entries.brief: One upright hourglass with two bulbs, narrow waist, top and base, and an integrated sand mound. No arrow or clock badge.
entries.why: A reusable time object; timeout is an alias, not a new drawing.

entries.name: Speedometer
entries.meaning: The speed of a website or service.
entries.brief: One gauge with a curved dial, sparse ticks, and an integrated needle. No browser frame or lightning badge.
entries.why: The source called Performance metrics is a browser frame; a gauge conveys speed directly.

entries.name: Funnel
entries.meaning: Filtering content or narrowing a selection.
entries.brief: One funnel with a broad open mouth tapering to a narrow spout. No stacked conversion stages or people.
entries.why: Use the recognizable object to avoid drawing an entire filtering interface.

entries.name: Magnet
entries.meaning: Attracting visitors and interest.
entries.brief: One horseshoe magnet with two integrated contrasting pole tips. No money, people, or floating attraction lines.
entries.why: A secondary metaphor for growth, shared with Design.
